claim_summaries.claim: Uniform Gaussian and N66 product-sensor tail truncation has TV cost O(tau) under an effective tail envelope and the stated ellipsoid/independence hypotheses.
For arbitrary coordinate-oracle sequences r_i -> 0, an effective active-mode cutoff cannot be computed uniformly; a halting-coded computable sequence gives a contradiction.
Finite digital randomness yields countable output support and TV distance one from continuous target laws, so the candidate stochastic kernels are not finite-bit TV implementations.
N31 geometric and polynomial bit asymptotics follow from its candidate S_r and N_r bounds; proof status remains conditional because the full linked package is absent.
Fisher spectra alone cannot determine the archive rate; the supplied analytic shared-scalar/product pair is a baseline counterexample.
N75's KLS-open label is stale against two Oct 4, 2026 primary arXiv preprints claiming full KLS proofs; correctness is unverified, and the separate likelihood-information transfer remains open.

next_gate: Specify effective spectrum/model oracles and output randomness metric; independently audit N31 scalar estimates and the N75 likelihood-information bound after reviewing Oct 4 KLS preprints.
